author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Ben Shelton reached his first U.S. Open final Friday night by defeating fellow American Frances Tiafoe 4-6, 6-3, 6-3, 7-5 at Arthur Ashe Stadium. After dropping the opening set, the 23-year-old took control through the middle of the match and broke late in the fourth to close the semifinal without a deciding set.

Shelton became the first Black American man to reach the U.S. Open final since Arthur Ashe in 1972 and the first to reach any men’s major final since MaliVai Washington at Wimbledon in 1996. He is also one victory from ending a 23-year wait for an American men’s Grand Slam singles champion, dating to Andy Roddick’s 2003 U.S. Open title.

Sunday’s championship match will pit Shelton against top seed Alexander Zverev. Zverev advanced by beating Karen Khachanov 6-3, 7-6(7), 7-6(6) and has not dropped a set in his last four matches. Shelton will bring a powerful serve and strong home support into the matchup, while Zverev enters with experience from multiple major finals and the 2026 French Open title.
dek: The 23-year-old won the all-American semifinal in four sets and will face Alexander Zverev for the title Sunday.
headline: Ben Shelton beats Frances Tiafoe to reach U.S. Open final
